sentences.text: This dinosaur is recognized by four unique derived traits, including a groove between the upper jaw bones.
Other distinct features include an elongated cheekbone with parallel edges and two small bumps located below the eye sockets.
The front of the upper jaw lacks teeth, possessing instead a horny edge for gripping food.
The cheekbone itself is formed into a distinct inverted T-shape.
Finally, the rear blade of the hip bone points obliquely.
The skeleton of this small ceratopsian was discovered on the westbank of the river Tuanhe in Neixiang, Henan.
The holotype specimen ZMNH M8856 was found in a layer of the Xiaguan Formation dating from the Turonian to Campanian stages.

The holotype is represented by an incomplete and disarticulated skeleton including pelvis and leg bones, twenty-four vertebrae, a dorsal rib, a humerus, a radius, and the anterior articulated part of the skull with disarticulated postorbital and squamosal bones.

The articulated part of the skull preserves the rostral bone, premaxilla, maxilla, jugal, quadratojugal, dentary, surangular, angular bone, anterior section of the prefrontal bone, and anterior part of the nasal bone.
Mosaiceratops lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 94 to 72 million years ago, from the Turonian to Campanian stages, in what is now Asia.
It is debated whether Mosaiceratops is the most basal neoceratopsian or the sister taxon to Psittacosaurus, which would reinstate the family name Psittacosauridae.
